name: Agent prose by the writing guide

pr.title: Write GitHub comments and issues an agent posts on its own by the writing guide
pr.head: b74ec10d9ce786d3ad5208fc81903a7a648c2ec7

summary: Projector ships a writing guide, skills/writing.md, and its skills, such as implement and fix-pr, read it before they write a pull request body, a commit message, or a reply. An agent also writes prose outside those skills: a reply to a reviewer, an issue it opens, a commit message for a change it makes by hand, or a comment in code it edits directly. Until now nothing pointed that prose at the guide.
This pull request closes the gap in two places:

1. The generated conventions block. project init writes a ## Projector conventions section into each repository's AGENTS.md from a template. The template, now version 33, gains a paragraph telling an agent to write that other prose with the write skill, whether or not the person asked for prose.
  2. The write skill's description. A host picks a skill by its description, so the description now says to use write for prose the agent writes on its own. That reaches Codex, and repositories whose block predates version 33.
The review found one open question: the write skill's final step still says not to post or commit text unless the user asks, which conflicts with the new trigger.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Conventions block: the section between projector:begin and projector:end markers that project init writes into AGENTS.md. Its integer is the template version.
  • Writing guide: skills/writing.md, the prose rules every Projector skill follows.
  • Pinned hash: a test records a hash of each template version, so the text cannot change without the version moving.

groups.title: When an agent uses the write skill
groups.kicker: The skill description that decides when a host invokes write
intro: Claude Code and Codex choose a skill by matching the task against each skill's description. The old description limited write to prose the user asked for, so an agent replying to a review comment on its own never reached for it. The new sentence adds prose the agent writes itself, outside a Projector skill that already applies the guide.

files.note: The description gains the on-its-own trigger; the skill body is unchanged.

checks.text: The skill's "Hand it over" section still ends "Do not commit, push, or post the text unless the user asks" and asks for a report of what changed. An agent that posts a reply or opens an issue on its own, the case this description now targets, either holds the text back or skips that step. The review asks for the hand-over to treat prose the agent writes as a step of its own task differently.

groups.title: The conventions block, version 33
groups.kicker: The template paragraph, the regenerated AGENTS.md, and the pinned hash
intro: The template's paragraph sits under "Projector skills", the part of the block that applies only where the plugin is installed, because the guide and the write skill ship with the plugin. The sentence about Google developer documentation style, earlier in the block, still applies everywhere.
AGENTS.md in this repository is the template's output, and CLAUDE.md is a symlink to it, so both diffs carry the same paragraph.

checks.text: The review's gate ran claude plugin validate, claude plugin test, and git diff --check, and the Check workflow, which runs the Python tests and project check, passed on this head. So the hash pinned for version 33 matches the template, and AGENTS.md is not stale.

files.note: The begin marker moves to 33 and the new paragraph follows the spec sentence.

checks.text: "The rest" means prose outside Projector's skills. The commit-message and pull-request-body clause repeats the exception for implement, spec, and fix-pr, which write those themselves.

files.note: Regenerated from the template; the same paragraph and version.
Pins the version 33 hash beside the earlier versions.

groups.title: Plugin documentation
groups.kicker: What docs/plugins.md says the write skill covers
intro: The plugin guide now says write covers both prose a person asks for and prose an agent writes on its own, with a reply to a review comment and an opened issue as examples.

files.note: One sentence widened to name prose an agent writes on its own.
